newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST - Hungary to halve foreign debt by 1998.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Hungary to halve foreign debt by 1998.

text.p: Hungary is likely to reduce its net foreign state debt to $5 billion by 1998 from the current $9.4 billion, Frigyes Harshegyi, Vice President of the National Bank of Hungary said on Monday.
Harshegyi was quoted by the daily Vilaggazdasag as saying that Hungary had reduced its net foreign debt, not including company debt, to $9.4 billion from $16.5 billion in 1990.
Its international increased to above $10 billion from a few hundred million dollars in the period.
Hungary's full foreign debt, including corporate debt, amounts to 13.7 billion, or some 80 percent of planned foreign currency revenues this year, Harshegyi added.
Harshegyi said the 80 percent rate would justify an 'A' credit rating for the country, which has been upgraded to 'BBB-' by Standard & Poor's recently.
